previous_assumption: Machine Model should be per-organization (each Rental Company maintains its own private model catalogue) — recommended to avoid shaping MVP around the deferred OEM domain and to avoid needing a platform-admin actor.
correction: Owner decided the opposite: FleetIP uses a platform-level Product Catalogue (ProductCategory -> Product), not per-organization models. Product is global/ownerless data with no organization_id; only Machine (the physical asset) is organization-owned and references a catalogue Product. This is deliberately structured so OEM catalogue participation can be added later (e.g. a nullable source_organization_id + review workflow on products) as an additive migration, without restructuring the Category->Product->Machine->Organization graph. MVP keeps Product/ProductCategory writes seed-only (migration-managed, no runtime API), which also sidesteps needing a platform-admin authorization concept until a real write endpoint requires one.
